findings.finding: Union authorship shrinks each voter's eligible set; tally turns a one-eligible-card ballot into a last-place vote and scores a card every voter co-wrote 0.0. Three two-author Lite candidates: ballots carry no signal, shuffle order ranks them.
findings.evidence: council.py:358 pts=(n-1-pos)/max(1,n-1) is 0 when n=1; council.py:376 avg is 0.0 when no ballot counts. Probe with the real tally(): three candidates authored {X,Y}, {Y,Z}, {X,Z}; three identical ballots, then three reversed ones: every card scores 0.0 both times, agreement 0.0, order = label order. A card written by all three experts and ranked first on every ballot scores 0.0. This run's five-card pool already holds a two-author card. Under A, listing fewer parents raises a card's score, so the chair gains by an incomplete record.
findings.fix: Fix tally first: one-eligible-card ballots add nothing; where exclusion leaves a card under two voters, count all ballots for it and log a deviation. Test the Lite three-author case.

findings.finding: Its premise is false: tally gives missing or unknown labels the bottom places, not a neutral rank. A repaired ballot that skipped or misspelt its top pick votes that card last, and only run.json records it.
findings.evidence: council.py:363-369: unranked labels share positions len(ranking)..n-1, i.e. the bottom (docstring: 'share the remaining places'). Probe with the real tally(), 10 labels: top pick omitted -> 0.000, rank 10 of 10, problems=[]; top pick written with a 'Candidate ' prefix -> 0.000, rank 10 of 10. Neither the ledger nor fuse-input shows repairs, so the flip is invisible to the chair.
findings.fix: Normalise label spelling (prefixes, case) before counting gaps; place repaired labels at the ballot's middle, not bottom; print repairs in the ledger. Test both cases.

findings.finding: ingest --force drops every invalid or unreturned seat, not just the one that failed twice. Printed while another seat is pending, it drops that seat too; in loop-1 ideate, the control arm for the whole run.
findings.evidence: run.py _collect (854, 874-875): with --force and quorum met, every entry in bad, including 'no output yet', is dropped; --force takes only a reason. Unreturned seats are never re-spawned by the ingest message ('Still waiting for'), so they sit at zero recorded failures. Probe (Lite, scratch project): one expert invalid, CTRL unreturned, --force citing only the expert -> control {'done': False}, and the deviation logs CTRL under the expert's reason. SKILL.md: 'Do what next prints, nothing more.'
findings.fix: Add ingest --drop <seat>: drops only named seats with two rejections in this phase, refusing while others are pending. Print that, never bare --force.

findings.finding: Demoting elder score gaps is not enough: ingest_elders indexes o['scores'][label] directly, so an elder that skips one card's scores passes validation, then crashes ingest with an uncaught KeyError after the costliest calls.
findings.evidence: run.py:1120 builds 'scores': {ident(l): o['scores'][l] for l in labels}; council.py main() catches only RunError (653-655). Probe (scratch project): v_elder score errors moved to warnings, one label deleted from an elder's scores -> uncaught KeyError; phase stays elders and no retry prompt is written.
findings.fix: Read scores with (o.get('scores') or {}).get(l, {}) in ingest_elders; unit-test an elder output missing a whole label and one missing a criterion.

findings.finding: Loop-1 shortlist votes always have more cards than voters (10-21 vs 7), so 'each card leads about equally often' cannot hold; rotating by seat index leaves 21 cards at mean positions 3 to 17, untested.
findings.evidence: run.py ingest_merge runs the vote only when the pool exceeds N+2 = 9; Full keeps up to 7 x 3 = 21 cards. Computed for 21 cards x 7 seats: offset = seat index gives per-card mean positions 3.0 to 17.0 (one shared order: 0 to 20); offset = seat x 21 // 7 gives 9.0 to 11.0. Only 7 of 21 cards can ever lead. Even spacing stays within cards/seats slots of the middle for every size from 3 to 21 cards and 5 to 7 seats; rotate-by-one does not.
findings.fix: Space offsets evenly (seat × cards // seats); test every card's mean position is within cards/seats slots of the middle, for 21 cards and 7 seats.

findings.finding: It trusts from and parents, which the chair still types: a merged card listing the wrong ref keeps the hole, and nothing checks that every kept card reached the pool, so a dropped direction goes unrecorded.
findings.evidence: run.py next_merge drafts from=[ref] per card for the chair to edit; no code compares the refs used in pool.json with the set of kept refs. next_merge already computes word overlap between cards (_tokens, Jaccard >= 0.25), which could compare each pool body with its listed sources. SKILL.md: keep every distinct direction. The ELI5 ('nobody can vote for their own') overclaims.
findings.fix: Require every kept ref in some pool card's from; warn when a pool body overlaps ≥25% with a kept card it does not list, reusing next_merge's word overlap.

findings.finding: After the move-aside, an ingest before dispatch lists those CLI seats as 'Still waiting for' with no dispatch line. CLI seats never arrive by waiting, so the stall returns in a new form.
findings.evidence: run.py _collect 863-869: only seats with a rejected file on disk get spawn lines; seats with none get 'Still waiting for'. Probe (scratch project, COUNCIL_SEATS_VIA=cli:claude): dispatch --dry-run after a rejection runs only the unreturned seat, confirming the dead end; then three rejected outputs renamed aside and ingest re-run -> 'Still waiting for: L1, L2, L3, CTRL', no RUN line. A never-dispatched CLI seat already shows the same today.
findings.fix: In _collect, print the dispatch command for missing seats whose via is cli or openrouter, not 'Still waiting for'; test it with the moved-aside case.

findings.finding: Suspected: labels stay fixed per phase, so any preference for a label token such as 'A' still lands on the same card in every ballot. C spreads position bias but leaves label bias summed by Borda.
findings.evidence: Zheng et al., ICLR 2024, 'Large Language Models Are Not Robust Multiple Choice Selectors', trace most option-selection bias to preference for option-ID tokens rather than position. Unverified for listwise ranking. Check: rank one packet twice with labels permuted and compare per-card Borda.
findings.fix: Give each seat its own label permutation too, kept in the private mapping; translate each ballot to canonical labels at ingest, before tally.

findings.finding: Suspected: if next and status validate through _collect, every call re-appends friction notes (retried ingests already duplicate them), and an attempt counter placed there turns two status calls into 'failed twice', triggering the --force line.
findings.evidence: run.py _collect 851-852 appends friction for each valid seat on every call and saves before raising (871). Probe: one failed ingest, then a forced one, left the same friction note twice in run.json. cmd_next saves run.json (475); cmd_status is read-only today.
findings.fix: Split a pure validate() out of _collect; record friction and count attempts only inside ingest; test that repeated status and next calls leave friction and attempt counts unchanged.

findings.finding: Suspected: the unit test can only mock providers.ask, and the codex and gemini adapters have never run, so the first real cross-lab retry likely fails upstream; with the dead end gone, nothing in the tool caps paid re-dispatches.
findings.evidence: Facts: codex and gemini CLI paths are written from docs and untested; a nested claude -p fails auth here. providers._command builds 'codex exec -o <file> -' and 'gemini -o json -p <nudge>'; no test runs a subprocess. run['retries'] (run.py:870) is one global counter that nothing reads.
findings.fix: Test with a fake codex script on PATH that answers prose then valid JSON, exercising dispatch, parse and retry; stop re-dispatching a seat after two rejections.

eli5: If the computer lists everyone who helped, a card everyone helped write gets no fair votes and loses.
friction: The packet does not say whether a pre-existing bug that a candidate amplifies (tally's zero scores under A) counts against that candidate; I treated it as yes.
